adummim_32.name: Adummim
adummim_32.what: An ascent on the road from Jericho up to Jerusalem, on the boundary between Judah and Benjamin.
adummim_32.today: Likely Tal'at ed-Damm, near Ma'ale Adummim east of Jerusalem
key: Judah's northern border turned toward Gilgal, opposite the ascent of Adummim (Joshua 15).
Benjamin's southern border also ran opposite the ascent of Adummim (Joshua 18).

beth-haccherem_209.name: Beth-haccherem
beth-haccherem_209.what: A town of Judah near Jerusalem that served as a district center and a place for signal fires.
beth-haccherem_209.today: Possibly Ramat Rahel, between Jerusalem and Bethlehem
key: Malchijah son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth-haccherem, repaired the Dung Gate (Nehemiah 3).
Jeremiah called for a signal raised over Beth-haccherem as disaster came from the north (Jeremiah 6).

bezek_245.name: Bezek
bezek_245.what: The place where Judah and Simeon defeated the Canaanites and Perizzites and captured Adoni-bezek.
bezek_245.today: Exact site unknown; possibly Khirbet Bezqa near Gezer
key: After Joshua's death, Judah and Simeon defeated ten thousand Canaanites and Perizzites at Bezek (Judges 1).
They fought Adoni-bezek there, pursued him, and cut off his thumbs and big toes (Judges 1).

colossae_305.name: Colossae
colossae_305.what: A city in the Lycus Valley of Asia Minor, home of the church to which Paul wrote Colossians.
colossae_305.today: Unexcavated mound near Honaz, Denizli Province, southwestern Turkey
key: Paul and Timothy wrote to the saints and faithful brothers in Christ at Colossae (Colossians 1).
The Colossians had learned the gospel from Epaphras, Paul's beloved fellow servant (Colossians 1).
Paul sent Tychicus with Onesimus, one of their own, to tell them his news (Colossians 4).
He asked that the letter also be read in the church of the Laodiceans (Colossians 4).

geruth_chimham_460.name: Geruth Chimham
geruth_chimham_460.what: A lodging place near Bethlehem where the remnant of Judah stopped on the way to Egypt.
key: After Gedaliah's murder, Johanan and the remnant stayed at Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem (Jeremiah 41).
They meant to go on to Egypt because they feared the Chaldeans (Jeremiah 41).

hammon_519.name: Hammon
hammon_519.what: A town on the border of Asher's inheritance in the far north, toward Sidon.
hammon_519.today: Possibly Umm el-Amed, near the coast of southern Lebanon
key: Hammon is listed with Ebron, Rehob, and Kanah on the boundary of Asher (Joshua 19).
From these towns Asher's border reached as far as Sidon the Great (Joshua 19).

kanah_667.name: Kanah
kanah_667.what: A town on the northern border of Asher's inheritance, toward Sidon.
kanah_667.today: Likely Qana, southeast of Tyre in southern Lebanon
key: Kanah is listed with Ebron, Rehob, and Hammon on the boundary of Asher (Joshua 19).
From these towns Asher's border reached as far as Sidon the Great (Joshua 19).

nicopolis_894.name: Nicopolis
nicopolis_894.what: A city where Paul decided to spend the winter, asking Titus to join him there.
nicopolis_894.today: Likely Nicopolis in Epirus, near Preveza, western Greece
key: Paul told Titus to come to him at Nicopolis once Artemas or Tychicus arrived (Titus 3).
Paul had decided to spend the winter there (Titus 3).

paphos_919.name: Paphos
paphos_919.what: A city on the southwest coast of Cyprus, seat of the Roman proconsul.
paphos_919.today: Paphos (Kato Paphos), on the southwest coast of Cyprus
key: Barnabas and Saul traveled through Cyprus from Salamis as far as Paphos (Acts 13).
There they met the magician Bar-Jesus and the proconsul Sergius Paulus (Acts 13).
When Elymas was struck blind, the proconsul believed (Acts 13).
From Paphos Paul and his companions set sail for Perga in Pamphylia (Acts 13).

tower_1180.name: Tower of the Ovens
tower_1180.what: A tower on Jerusalem's wall, repaired in Nehemiah's day and passed by a choir at the wall's dedication.
tower_1180.today: Exact site unknown; on the western side of ancient Jerusalem
key: Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab repaired the Tower of the Ovens (Nehemiah 3).
At the wall's dedication, one thanksgiving choir passed the Tower of the Ovens to the Broad Wall (Nehemiah 12).

zarethan_1243.name: Zarethan
zarethan_1243.what: A town in the Jordan Valley near Adam, where the Jordan's waters stopped for Israel's crossing.
zarethan_1243.today: Exact site unknown; possibly Tell es-Saidiyeh, east of the Jordan
key: The Jordan's waters stood in a heap at Adam, the city beside Zarethan, as Israel crossed (Joshua 3).
Baana's district under Solomon included Beth-shean, beside Zarethan (1 Kings 4).
Solomon's bronze temple furnishings were cast in clay ground between Succoth and Zarethan (1 Kings 7).
